newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent hovers near day's low, awaits NYMEX.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent hovers near day's low, awaits NYMEX.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures hovered near the day's low on Monday due to some follow-through selling from Friday and a lethargic market ahead of the NYMEX open, dealers said.
March Brent traded 14 cents lower at $22.38 a barrel at 1320 GMT, just off the intra-day low of $22.35.

"It's been hovering around the $22.40 area all day and dipped below it when the States on ACCESS (after-hours trading system) went down on their March WTI, so I think all eyes from Europe are watching what the Americans are going to do," one dealer said.
Brokers attributed Monday's falls to technical weakness and a continuation of Friday's sell-off following last week's mid-week rally.

"We've been stuck around the same area all morning. To all intents and purposes the market is fairly quiet, but if anything there's a little bit of follow-through selling from Friday's session," another dealer said.
February gas oil traded at $205 a tonne, down $4.25 in line with brokers expectations and a weather-inspired weak finish in the United States for heating oil (NYMEX) on Friday.
Weather Services Corp, a private forecaster, predicted average to above average temperatures over the next few days for the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market.
Some brokers said the market could test recent lows again at the end of the range, but said with a lack of market-moving news very little was happening.
